around.headline: Karnataka's health minister confirms relabelled, counterfeit medicines reached hospitals and ICUs
around.summary: Officials confirmed today that medicines carrying forged MNC labels — tied to the Rs 5-crore Bidadi raid — had reached hospitals, pharmacies and even ICUs statewide, with a fresh Bengaluru raid seizing Rs 3.38 crore of expired and counterfeit stock. If you or a family member is on regular medication, buy only from a licensed pharmacy and verify the batch number if anything about a strip feels off.

around.headline: Bengaluru school served corporation notice after 500+ students fall sick with H1N1
around.summary: A Bengaluru school's mass illness — initially blamed on street vendors — was identified as an H1N1 outbreak, prompting the civic corporation to issue a notice. If your child's school is affected, don't wait for an official circular: report symptoms directly and keep a feverish child home until fever-free for 24 hours.
around.source: The Hindu, NDTV, The Times of India

around.headline: Bengaluru firms oppose mandatory WFH tied to ORR roadworks, want Metro prioritised instead
around.summary: Tech firms are pushing back on a proposed mandatory work-from-home order meant to ease congestion during the ORR's Rs 450-crore white-topping work, arguing the city should prioritise Metro capacity instead. If you commute the ORR corridor, expect this dispute to keep shaping when the roadworks actually start.
around.source: The Indian Express, Moneycontrol, BW People

around.headline: Metro Blue Line Phase 2A trials expected from October; Silk Board-adjacent stations delayed to March 2027
around.summary: Trial runs on the Phase 2A stretch should begin in October, but two stations near the Silk Board corridor won't open until March 2027. Don't plan your ORR-to-Metro switch around this stretch any time soon.

around.headline: GBA makes registered structural engineers mandatory for builders
around.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has directed builders to compulsorily engage registered structural engineers for new construction, tightening oversight after recent building-safety lapses. If you're building or renovating, this is now a compliance requirement, not just good practice.

around.headline: At least nine killed in a Kolkata hotel fire
around.summary: A hotel fire in Kolkata killed at least nine people today. A timely reminder to check fire exits and extinguisher locations whenever you check into any hotel, in Bengaluru or elsewhere.

around.headline: Nifty, Sensex slide as 112 stocks hit 52-week lows
around.summary: Markets fell today with 112 NSE-listed stocks — including HDFC Bank, ITC and HUL — touching 52-week lows. If you hold SIPs or direct equity, a broad-based dip like this is a cue to review your allocation rather than react to a single day's move.

street_smart.title: Your child comes home with fever and body ache the same day news breaks that 500+ students at a Bengaluru school have fallen sick with flu-like symptoms — your own school hasn't sent any notice yet. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a Bengaluru school's mass illness among 500+ students — first blamed on street vendors — was identified as an H1N1 outbreak, prompting the civic corporation to serve the school a notice (The Hindu, NDTV, The Times of India). This is a fresh angle on the story — a parent's at-home decision-making during a school outbreak — not covered as street-smart in the last 3 weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: Your child is running a mild-to-moderate fever with body ache and a cough, but seems otherwise alert and is eating normally. School reopens tomorrow and hasn't sent any communication about illness in class, even though outbreak news is already circulating.

choices.text: Keep your child home, give fluids and paracetamol for the fever, watch for warning signs, and inform the school directly so they can track and isolate cases — see a doctor if fever crosses 2 days or breathing looks laboured.
choices.feedback: Correct. In this case, the school only acted after the corporation stepped in with a notice — schools often lag on formal communication, so a parent reporting symptoms directly is what actually surfaces a cluster early and triggers a proper civic response, rather than waiting for a circular that may never come in time.

choices.text: Assume it's just the usual monsoon cold — like the school first assumed it was food from street vendors — and send your child back to school the next morning once the fever seems to have broken.
choices.feedback: This mirrors exactly what delayed containment here: the illness was first waved off as vendor food poisoning before it was identified as H1N1. A fever that only 'seems' broken can recur, a common flu pattern, and sending a child back too soon re-exposes classmates. The rule is fever-free for a full 24 hours before return, not fever-free at a glance.

choices.text: Rush to the nearest hospital emergency room for a full check-up and flu test right away, even though there's no breathing difficulty or other red-flag symptom.
choices.feedback: Mild fever with body ache and no breathing trouble or lethargy doesn't need an ER visit — most flu, including H1N1 in an otherwise healthy child, is manageable at home like any bad flu. Save the ER for red flags: fever beyond 2 days, breathing difficulty, or unusual drowsiness — using it for every mild case adds strain exactly when a real outbreak needs capacity for serious cases.

choices.text: Give a leftover course of antibiotics from a previous illness 'just in case,' so the fever comes down faster.
choices.feedback: Antibiotics don't work on flu viruses like H1N1 at all — this only delays proper care while masking how the illness is actually progressing, and repeated misuse like this is exactly how antibiotic resistance builds up. Paracetamol for fever, fluids, rest, and a doctor's call if it worsens is the actual playbook.

takeaways: Don't wait for a school circular once outbreak news is already public — report your child's symptoms directly so the school (or corporation, if needed) can track and isolate cases before they spread further.
Flu-like illness, H1N1 or otherwise: rest, fluids, and paracetamol for fever; only return to school after a full 24 hours fever-free, not just when the fever 'seems' gone.
Reserve antibiotics and ER visits for real red flags — fever beyond 2 days, breathing difficulty, or unusual lethargy — not as a default response to an ordinary flu-like fever.

quiz.question: What outbreak led Bengaluru's civic corporation to issue a notice to a school today, after 500+ students fell sick?
quiz.why: The illness was initially blamed on food from street vendors before being identified as H1N1 — a reminder that the first explanation for a cluster of illness isn't always the right one.

quiz.question: Bengaluru firms today opposed a proposed mandatory work-from-home order tied to which project?
quiz.why: Firms now want the city to prioritise Metro capacity instead of mandating WFH during the roadworks — a shift from earlier reports of companies themselves floating WFH as their preferred fix.

quiz.question: At least how many people were killed in a hotel fire in Kolkata reported today?
quiz.why: Hotel fires are a recurring monsoon-season risk due to electrical faults — always locate the nearest fire exit and extinguisher when you check in anywhere.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's drinking water is drawn from the Cauvery river, whose source lies in which part of Karnataka?
quiz.why: Kodagu's dense forests and heavy rainfall feed the river at its source — which is also why deforestation there can affect Bengaluru's water supply decades downstream.

quiz.question: In stock market terms, what does it mean when a stock hits a '52-week low' — as 112 stocks did on the NSE today?
options: Its lowest traded price in the past year
Its lowest trading volume of the week
A stock about to be delisted
quiz.why: It's a purely price-based technical marker, not a verdict on a company's fundamentals — some investors watch 52-week lows for potential value buys, others treat them as a caution sign.
